title: Lubricated Bolts and Reduced Torque
description: Lubrication effect on bolt tension and torque. Calculate the reduced torque required for lubricated bolts compared to dry bolts.

components.content:
### Example - Reduction of Torque when Bolt is Lubricated

The maximum tightening torque for a slightly lubricated 1" Grade 5 coarse bolt is _483 lbf ft_. Dry bolt torque is approximately 30% higher - or _628 lbf ft_.

_Tdry = (483 lbf ft) (1 + (30%) / (100%))_

   _= 628 lbf ft_

If the bolt is lubricated with SAE 30 oil - the torque compared to a dry bolt is reduced with approximately _40%_.

_TSAE30 = (628 lbf ft) (1 - (40%) / (100%))_

   _= 377 lbf ft_

**Note:** If torque specified for a dry or slightly oiled bolt is applied to a lubricated bolt - the bolt may overload and break.
